concept.tagline: Automated testing and scoring pipelines measuring LLM accuracy, safety, latency, and cost across golden datasets before every release.
concept.purpose: Replace ad-hoc 'vibe checks' with a three-tier evaluation harness combining deterministic assertions, reference metrics, and calibrated LLM-as-a-judge rubrics.

spark.summary: An automated testing and scoring pipeline that measures LLM accuracy, safety, latency, and cost across curated datasets before and after every prompt, model, or retrieval change.
spark.keyTakeaway: Replace 'vibe checks' with a versioned golden dataset, deterministic code assertions, calibrated LLM-as-a-judge rubrics, and statistical confidence gates in CI/CD.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** An **LLM evaluation harness** is a versioned test runner that executes a prompt, RAG pipeline, or agent against a curated **golden dataset** (typically 200–500 stratified examples) and computes pass/fail gates across quality, latency, and cost.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Three-Tier Evaluation Gate Before Prompt Promotion (CI Runner -> LLM Pipeline -> Code Assertions -> LLM Judge); PR Gate -> Nightly Shadow Suite -> Human Calibration Store (PR CI Gate -> Nightly Replay -> Pinned Judge -> Human Audit).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance statistical precision against CI feedback speed and judge token cost. LLM outputs are stochastic, and a prompt edit that fixes one edge case routinely breaks three others silently.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Connect automated LLM evaluation to canary rollouts, prompt design, and LoRA distillation.

learningJourney.title: What is an LLM Evaluation Harness
learningJourney.explanation:
An **LLM evaluation harness** is a versioned test runner that executes a prompt, RAG pipeline, or agent against a curated **golden dataset** (typically 200–500 stratified examples) and computes pass/fail gates across quality, latency, and cost.

Evaluation is organized into three tiers: **deterministic code assertions** (JSON Schema, regex, SQL execution), **reference-based metrics** (exact match, F1, semantic similarity), and **calibrated LLM-as-a-judge rubrics**.

sectionDiagram.summary: Fast deterministic checks fail broken schemas immediately before spending judge tokens on nuanced faithfulness scoring.

learningJourney.title: Why prompt edits silently break production
learningJourney.explanation:
LLM outputs are stochastic, and a prompt edit that fixes one edge case routinely breaks three others silently. Without an evaluation harness, teams ship regressions in JSON formatting, hallucinated citations, or latency spikes directly to users—only discovering them via support tickets.

In multi-step agent pipelines, silent 5% per-component regressions compound into broken end-to-end workflows.

ideas.title: Mitigating Judge Position & Verbosity Bias
ideas.description: LLM judges prefer the first option in pairwise A/B comparisons by 5–15% and favor longer answers. Randomize A/B order and score against explicit binary/Likert rubrics.

ideas.title: Preventing Eval Contamination
ideas.description: Maintain a held-out production shadow set refreshed monthly from real logs and never place held-out examples inside few-shot prompts.

learningJourney.explanation: Run evaluation suites at every boundary where model behavior, retrieval, or prompt templates change.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Prompt, Model & RAG Changes
benefits: Quantifies accuracy/latency deltas before upgrading models (e.g., frontier to distilled 8B) or tweaking chunk sizes.
costs: Requires curating and maintaining 200–500 stratified golden examples.

benefits: Catches tool-argument drift and trajectory regressions across multi-turn traces.
costs: Multi-turn agent evals can take 10–20 minutes on full nightly suites.

benefits: Standard unit/integration tests give 100% exact verification for arithmetic, regexes, and SQL.
costs: Using an LLM judge for deterministic logic wastes money and adds variance.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Implementing a Position-Debiased Pairwise Eval Runner
learningJourney.explanation: Run deterministic schema checks first, then run a pinned judge model with CoT-before-score and swapped A/B ordering to cancel position bias.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Code Assertions vs. LLM-as-a-Judge vs. CI Slices
learningJourney.explanation: Balance statistical precision against CI feedback speed and judge token cost.

benefits: Instant, free, and 100% reproducible for JSON Schema, AST parse, and tool-call match.
costs: Cannot evaluate open-ended tone, faithfulness, or nuanced reasoning.

benefits: Runs in 1–3 minutes on every PR to block obvious regressions.
costs: Wider confidence intervals on rare edge-case cohorts.

benefits: Narrows 95% confidence intervals to ±1–2% to catch subtle regressions.
costs: 20+ minute runtime and higher API spend.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Continuous Shadow Eval & Judge Calibration Loop
learningJourney.explanation: Production teams separate a fast **PR Gate** (200 stratified cases) from a **Nightly Shadow Replay** (sampled production traffic) and calibrate the pinned LLM judge monthly against 50–100 human-labeled examples (tracking Cohen's kappa).

sectionDiagram.title: PR Gate -> Nightly Shadow Suite -> Human Calibration Store

cards.label: 1. Pin Judge Snapshot
cards.detail: Never point evals at floating 'latest' model aliases that silently shift scoring baselines.

cards.label: 2. Stratified Cohorts
cards.detail: Tag cases by difficulty, language, and past incident IDs to prevent aggregate averages from hiding regressions.

cards.label: 3. Production Flywheel
cards.detail: Promote user thumbs-down traces into the golden dataset every week.

sectionDiagram.summary: A calibrated judge + stratified golden dataset turns subjective prompt tuning into measurable engineering.

knowledgeCheck.question: How do you prevent position bias when using an LLM-as-a-judge for pairwise A/B output comparison?

options.text: Always place the new candidate model in Position A
options.feedback: Placing the candidate consistently in Position A lets the 5–15% position bias inflate or deflate its score.

options.text: Run each comparison twice with A/B order swapped and average or require consistency across both passes
options.feedback: Correct: swapping A/B presentation order cancels out systematic first-position preference.

options.text: Use a floating 'latest' model alias for the judge
options.feedback: Floating aliases cause silent baseline drift over time; always pin judge snapshots.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
